claims.text: Standard cast HfNbTaTiZr has a randomly occupied multi-element lattice.
The randomly occupied lattice in standard cast HfNbTaTiZr produces intrinsic lattice distortions.
Intrinsic lattice distortions are directly responsible for the elevated-temperature nonlinear stress–strain behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Intrinsic lattice distortions are directly responsible for the elevated-temperature thermal-expansion behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
Intrinsic lattice distortions are directly responsible for the elevated-temperature elastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr.
In situ diffraction under mechanical loading can reveal the proposed relationship between intrinsic lattice distortion and macroscopic mechanical behavior.
Heating and loading produce temperature-dependent lattice distortions and evolution of atomic-scale elastic constants.
Intrinsic lattice distortion couples thermal expansion to elastic moduli in HfNbTaTiZr.
The coupling between thermal expansion and elastic moduli causes lattice parameters to vary nonlinearly with temperature.
Anharmonic atomic interactions become significant near 700–800°C.
Early defect rearrangements become significant near 700–800°C.
The 700–800°C regime marks a transition from elastic behavior to incipient plasticity.
In situ measurements will show nonlinear evolution of lattice parameters with temperature relative to ex situ baseline measurements.
In situ measurements will show nonlinear evolution of elastic moduli with temperature relative to ex situ baseline measurements.
A slope change or discontinuity in lattice-parameter evolution will occur around 700–800°C.
The lattice-parameter anomaly around 700–800°C will coincide with a measurable change in stress–strain response.
Coincidence of the lattice-parameter anomaly and stress–strain change indicates the onset of incipient plasticity.
The proposed behavior should hold from 25°C to 1000°C, from elastic loading through the threshold of plasticity, in an inert atmosphere.
The experiment will heat HfNbTaTiZr from 25°C to 1000°C while collecting synchrotron diffraction and stress–strain data under controlled loading.
Absence of a lattice-parameter slope change or discontinuity near 700–800°C that coincides with a stress–strain change would falsify the proposed coupling.
